page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors running at 3.3 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 32 dedicated physical CPU cores without simultaneous multithreading, matching a total count of 32 vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1900 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU balance and dedicated physical core architecture provide consistent compute throughput per thread for CPU-bound applications. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage eliminates network-attached storage latency for local read and write operations, enhancing resource density for input/output intensive scratch operations. Because local instance storage is ephemeral, applications requiring long-term data persistence must use secondary storage solutions. The c9gd.8xlarge is suitable for batch processing pipelines, software compilation, ad tech workload execution, and local caching servers.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 32 dedicated arm64 AWS Graviton processor cores operating at 3.3 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), it exhibits a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio suited for compute-heavy processing. The instance features 1900 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 17 Gbps. The combination of dedicated physical cores and integrated high-speed local storage yields stable single-core execution with low-latency local disk I/O, making it cost-efficient for core-bound workloads. Because the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, stateful applications must implement replication or external persistence. The c9gd.8xlarge is best suited for compute-intensive tasks requiring local scratch storage, including batch log processing, high-throughput web serving, ad tech pipelines, and local caching nodes.
